pull_request.body:
> Rebased on main after #34008 merged — this PR now carries only the Sana changes (kernel generalization + wiring).

## Motivation

Sana's transformer runs the eager adaLN chain `LN(x) * (1 + scale) + shift` at
41 sites per DiT forward (norm1/norm2 in each of the 20 blocks + the final
`SanaModulatedNorm`), as 4 aten kernels per site (affine-free LayerNorm,
`1+scale` row op, broadcast mul, broadcast add) — and because the DiT
propagates the patch-embed/GLUMBConv `permute` layout, the LayerNorm pays a
hidden layout-copy on every call as well. Elementwise ops are ~51% of Sana's
per-step GPU time, and no existing fusion applies: the CuTe-DSL
norm+scale+shift family needs `hidden % 256 == 0`, while Sana's hidden is
2240 (70 heads x 32).

PR #34008 introduced a Triton kernel replicating torch's aten
`vectorized_layer_norm_kernel` numerics bit for bit (serial Welford in aten's
element order, guarded-rcp fast path, shfl.down combine tree, MUFU.RSQ, plus
the per-op bf16 rounding of the modulate chain), so the fusion needs no
quality gate. That kernel assumed `hidden % 512 == 0` (all 128 aten threads
run the same vector count).

## Changes

1. **Kernel** (`layernorm_modulate.py`)
   - Support any `hidden % 4 == 0` (aten's own vectorization requirement) via
     a masked partial tail chunk: aten threads whose next vector index
     `i*128 + t` reaches `N/4` skip the iteration and enter the warp fold
     with a smaller Welford count. The `hidden % 512 == 0` path compiles
     exactly as before (GLM-Image regression tests stay green).
   - `fused_layernorm_modulate_raw`: direct-call variant without the
     `torch.ops` dispatch (~40 us CPU per call). The registered custom op
     now wraps the raw function; GLM-Image call sites are unchanged.
   - num_warps heuristic extended to 4 from hidden >= 2048 (H200-tuned:
     14.3 us vs the 43.1 us eager chain at Sana's (2, 1024, 2240)).

2. **Sana** (`sana.py`): route the three LN+modulate sites through the fused
   kernel, but **only in CUDA-graph contexts** — under stream capture or on
   a non-default stream (which is where the breakable-CUDA-graph runner
   (#33989) warms up and captures). Each new input signature
   (shape/stride/dtype/eps) is `torch.equal`-verified against the live eager
   chain during the BCG warmup iterations (non-capturing, so the sync is
   legal); capture then records the fused kernel; any mismatch permanently
   falls back to eager (#34008 recipe).

   Default-stream eager serving deliberately keeps the eager chain: Sana's
   eager mode is CPU-launch bound, and one Triton launch costs more Python
   time than the whole 5-deep aten enqueue pipeline it replaces — an
   in-process alternating A/B on the real model measured +14% forward wall
   when fusing eagerly, despite -4.8% GPU kernel time. Under BCG replay the
   Python launch cost is zero and the GPU saving is realized in full.

   The wrapper also issues an explicit `x.contiguous()` (the same copy
   aten's LayerNorm performs internally for Sana's transposed activations),
   keeping the fused site at 2 kernels vs the eager 5.

## Correctness (H200, torch 2.11.0+cu130)

- Standalone sweep: `torch.equal` at D=2240 (tail path), 4096/2560
  (GLM-Image regression), 3072 (FLUX.1), 1536/708/452; batch 1/2;
  seq 1..4096 — all bit-exact.
- Unit tests: new `test_sana_ln_modulate.py` (4 cases: real serving shapes
  incl. the transposed layout; asserts eager serving stays on the eager
  chain and the fusion verifies + engages on the capture-stream path) +
  existing `test_glm_image_ln_modulate.py` = 10 passed.
- e2e md5: output PNGs bit-identical to main in every paired round, both
  configs (10 rounds x 10 images compared), plus a 2-prompt x 2-seed
  4-arm check.
- Trace audit: the eager arm is kernel-for-kernel identical to main
  (11136 launches, 0 fused); the BCG arm replays 492 fused launches and 0
  aten LN per 5-step window.

## Performance

GPU-side attribution (torch profiler, 5 denoise steps = 12 DiT forwards):

| arm | total GPU kernel | launches | aten LN | fused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main BCG | 137.03 ms | 10932 | 492 | 0 |
| this PR BCG | 130.37 ms (-4.9%) | 9456 (-13.5%) | 0 | 492 |

(4 kernels per site -> 1 Triton kernel + the layout copy both arms already
paid.)

e2e, BCG config (protocol below): **denoise 405.2 -> 385.9 ms/request
(-4.8%)**, reproduced in 8/8 order-balanced paired rounds with spread
[-4.6%, -4.9%] across two builds. With denoise at ~55% of request e2e
(~0.74 s), this is ~-2.6% e2e. Wall/e2e/decode medians on this box swing
+-10-35% between *identical* binaries due to co-tenant load (measured with
a trace-identical build), so the graph-replayed denoise ratio is the
reliable metric; md5 identity plus the kernel-level trace deltas above are
the ground truth.

Eager config: unchanged by construction (trace-identical to main).

## Benchmark configuration

- H200 (ion8, shared box), torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
- `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers`, 1024x1024,
  seed 42, 20 steps (default preset), num_gpus=1, torch.compile off
- BCG arms: `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024`
- 10 back-to-back requests per round in one warmed process, drop first,
  median of 9; rounds run interleaved main/PR in both orders (main-first
  and PR-first) to cancel co-tenant drift; per-round paired deltas
- md5 of every saved PNG compared main vs PR per round

## Dependency

Depends on #34008 — this branch contains its commit; the kernel file and
GLM-Image wiring come from there. New in this PR: the tail-chunk
generalization, the raw direct-call variant, the warp heuristic, and the
Sana wiring.

## Follow-up (FLUX.1, #34004)

The generalized kernel is bit-exact at FLUX.1's hidden=3072 too. Measured on
top of the #34004 branch at the FLUX image-stream shape (1, 4096, 3072):

| variant | time | bit-exact |
|---|---|---|
| eager 4-kernel chain | 87.7 us | ref |
| #34004 lossless (aten LN + fused modulate) | 38.4 us | yes |
| #34004 quality=high folded-affine LN | 27.2 us | no (maxdiff 1.3e-1) |
| this kernel, single launch | 23.8 us | yes |

i.e. it strictly dominates the quality=high folded site while staying
lossless (at the (1, 512, 3072) text stream it ties: 23.7 vs 19.5/25.0 us).
Caveat before wiring it there: FLUX eager serving needs the same
CPU-launch-bound check that gated Sana (Sana lesson: a Triton launch can
cost more Python than the aten chain it replaces).

+def _sana_ln_modulate(
+    norm: nn.LayerNorm,
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: torch.Tensor,
+    shift: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Single-kernel ``LN(x) * (1 + scale) + shift``, bit-exact vs eager.
+
+    ``scale`` / ``shift`` are Sana's ``(batch, 1, dim)`` adaLN rows.  Each
+    new input signature is verified with ``torch.equal`` against the eager
+    chain (bit-exactness depends on which LayerNorm kernel aten dispatches
+    to); any mismatch disables the fast path permanently.
+
+    The fusion only engages in CUDA-graph contexts (stream capture, or the
+    non-default stream the breakable-CUDA-graph runner warms up and captures
+    on, #33989), where replay pays no Python launch cost.  Sana's eager mode
+    is CPU-launch bound and one Triton launch costs more Python than the
+    whole aten chain it replaces (+14% forward wall), so default-stream
+    serving keeps the eager chain.
+
+    ``x`` reaches every site transposed (patch-embed / GLUMBConv permute
+    layout); aten's LayerNorm contiguizes internally, and the fast path
+    issues the same copy explicitly.
+    """
+    global _SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_DISABLED
+
+    if _SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_DISABLED or torch.compiler.is_compiling() or not x.is_cuda:
+        return _eager_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+
+    capturing = torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+    if not capturing and torch.cuda.current_stream() == torch.cuda.default_stream():
+        return _eager_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+
+    sig = (
+        x.shape,
+        x.stride(),
+        x.dtype,
+        scale.shape,
+        scale.stride(),
+        shift.stride(),
+        norm.eps,
+    )
+    if sig in _SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_OK_SIGS:
+        return fused_layernorm_modulate_raw(
+            x.contiguous(), scale[:, 0], shift[:, 0], norm.eps
+        )
+    if capturing:
+        # unverified signature during capture: cannot sync-verify here
+        return _eager_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+
+    if (
+        x.dtype is torch.bfloat16
+        and x.dim() == 3
+        and scale.dim() == 3
+        and scale.shape[1] == 1
+        and shift.shape == scale.shape
+        and is_plain_layer_norm(norm, x.shape[-1])
+    ):
+        x_c = x.contiguous()
+        if not can_use_fused_layernorm_modulate(x_c, scale[:, 0], shift[:, 0]):
+            return _eager_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+        try:
+            out = fused_layernorm_modulate_raw(x_c, scale[:, 0], shift[:, 0], norm.eps)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            logger.warning_once(f"Disabling Sana fused LN+modulate fast path: {exc}")
+            _SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_DISABLED = True
+        else:

+            if torch.equal(out, ref):

+                return out
+            logger.warning_once(

+                "this platform's LayerNorm dispatch; falling back to eager"
+            )
+            _SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_DISABLED = True

+    return _eager_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)

+"""Sana fused LN+modulate fast path must stay bit-exact vs eager."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits.sana as sana
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits.sana import (
+    _eager_ln_modulate,
+    _sana_ln_modulate,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=3, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shape,nmod,transposed",
+    [
+        ((2, 1024, 2240), 6, False),
+        ((2, 1024, 2240), 2, False),
+        ((1, 1024, 2240), 6, True),
+        ((1, 37, 2240), 6, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_sana_fused_ln_modulate_is_bit_exact(shape, nmod, transposed):
+    # (., 1024, 2240) is the real Sana 1024px shape; hidden 2240 % 512 != 0
+    # exercises the kernel's partial tail chunk.  nmod mirrors the two adaLN
+    # chunk layouts, transposed the permuted layout the Sana DiT serves.
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    batch, seq, hidden = shape
+    norm = torch.nn.LayerNorm(hidden, eps=1e-6, elementwise_affine=False).cuda()
+    x = (torch.randn(batch, seq, hidden, device="cuda") * 4).bfloat16()
+    if transposed:
+        x = x.permute(0, 2, 1).contiguous().permute(0, 2, 1)
+    emb = torch.randn(batch, nmod, hidden, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    shift, scale = emb.chunk(nmod, dim=1)[0], emb.chunk(nmod, dim=1)[-1]
+    # default-stream eager serving must stay on the untouched eager chain
+    n_sigs = len(sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_OK_SIGS)
+    _sana_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+    assert len(sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_OK_SIGS) == n_sigs
+    # the fusion engages on non-default streams (the BCG warmup/capture path)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream()):
+        out = _sana_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+        assert len(sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_OK_SIGS) == n_sigs + 1  # verified
+        out2 = _sana_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)  # verified-sig lane
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, _eager_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift))
+    assert torch.equal(out2, out) and not sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_DISABLED
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))

+"""Sana fused LN+modulate fast path must stay bit-exact vs eager."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits.sana as sana
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits.sana import (
+    _eager_ln_modulate,
+    _sana_ln_modulate,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=3, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shape,nmod,transposed",
+    [
+        ((2, 1024, 2240), 6, False),
+        ((2, 1024, 2240), 2, False),
+        ((1, 1024, 2240), 6, True),
+        ((1, 37, 2240), 6, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_sana_fused_ln_modulate_is_bit_exact(shape, nmod, transposed):
+    # (., 1024, 2240) is the real Sana 1024px shape; hidden 2240 % 512 != 0
+    # exercises the kernel's partial tail chunk.  nmod mirrors the two adaLN
+    # chunk layouts, transposed the permuted layout the Sana DiT serves.
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    batch, seq, hidden = shape
+    norm = torch.nn.LayerNorm(hidden, eps=1e-6, elementwise_affine=False).cuda()
+    x = (torch.randn(batch, seq, hidden, device="cuda") * 4).bfloat16()
+    if transposed:
+        x = x.permute(0, 2, 1).contiguous().permute(0, 2, 1)
+    emb = torch.randn(batch, nmod, hidden, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    shift, scale = emb.chunk(nmod, dim=1)[0], emb.chunk(nmod, dim=1)[-1]
+    # default-stream eager serving must stay on the untouched eager chain
+    n_sigs = len(sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_OK_SIGS)
+    _sana_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+    assert len(sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_OK_SIGS) == n_sigs
+    # the fusion engages on non-default streams (the BCG warmup/capture path)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream()):
+        out = _sana_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)
+        assert len(sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_OK_SIGS) == n_sigs + 1  # verified
+        out2 = _sana_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift)  # verified-sig lane
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(out, _eager_ln_modulate(norm, x, scale, shift))
+    assert torch.equal(out2, out) and not sana._SANA_FUSED_LN_MOD_DISABLED
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))
